children: ) recorded its largest-ever single-day put options trading volume by dollar notional value last Friday.
The index reached an estimated $3.3T-$3.4T, according to market data.
The surge represented roughly a 330% increase above the 2024 average, with approximately 4.1M to 4.98M S&P 500 (
) put contracts traded compared to a three-month average of around 2.4M.
The put-to-call ratio spiked to 1.46 as investors aggressively bought downside protection heading into the close.
Goldman Sachs analysts characterized the trading session as a significant shift in market sentiment.

"Friday was the first real sign of panic in index protection, following weeks of significant damage in individual stocks," analysts said, adding that total put volume was the fourth highest back to 2015.
"A clear indication of just how much concern has built around broader index downside."

title: The S&P 500 had its largest ever put volume day on Friday
